faq.question: How much time does self-managing one NJ rental take?
faq.answer: Plan on 5 to 8 hours a month in steady state, plus 15 to 25 hours in any year with a turnover — roughly 90 to 120 hours per unit per year.

faq.question: What does a property manager typically charge in New Jersey?
faq.answer: Most NJ companies charge 8% to 12% of monthly collected rent, plus a one-time leasing fee when a tenant is placed. Ask whether the percentage applies to rent collected or rent due, and get the full fee schedule in writing.

faq.question: Is a property manager worth it for a single unit?
faq.answer: Often, yes — if you live far from the property, cannot take calls during work hours, or own in a rent-controlled municipality. If you are local, handy, and have the time, self-managing one unit can be the better deal.
